name: Residency Certificate for Persons of Independent Means

requirements.blocker_text: Reported requirement of a continuous source of annual income of CI$120,000 (approx. US$146,341), for Grand Cayman; not independently confirmed against the governing regulation's text in this pass.
requirements.fix_path: Demonstrate a continuous source of annual income of at least CI$120,000.

requirement_groups.name: Asset deposit plus real estate investment

requirements.blocker_text: Reported requirement of a minimum deposit of at least CI$400,000 in assets, plus a total investment in Grand Cayman of at least CI$1,000,000 (approx. US$1,200,000), of which at least CI$500,000 (approx. US$610,000) must be in developed real estate; not independently confirmed against the governing regulation's text in this pass.
requirements.fix_path: Hold the required asset deposit and make the required real estate investment.

evidence_required.document: Proof of income, assets, or real estate investment as applicable

sources.title: Cayman Islands Immigration (Transition) Act (2022 Revision) -- Sections 41-46: confirms the Residency Certificate for Persons of Independent Means exists, with revocation grounds for fraud or failure to maintain eligibility, but does not itself state the income/asset thresholds in the text extracted
Ogier (offshore law firm) -- Securing Cayman Residency via Independent Means or Direct Investment: reported income/asset thresholds and fee schedule

notes: STATUS: DRAFT, part of the Cayman Islands' initial build. The Immigration (Transition) Act confirms this certificate exists (Sections 41-46) but the specific income/asset thresholds are set by subsidiary regulation, not the Act itself, and that regulation's text was not reachable at tier-1 in this pass -- the official immigration.gov.ky domain that historically hosted this page returned a DNS failure, consistent with the gov.ky redesign that moved immigration services to the my.egov.ky/WORC portal. The figures here instead come from Ogier, a well-regarded offshore law firm, which is a stronger tier-3 source than a marketing blog but still not government-published -- hence draft status. Modelled as two OR-groups (passive income vs. asset-deposit-plus-real-estate) since the source frames them as alternative qualifying paths, not cumulative requirements. work_rights is 'none': this certificate is explicitly a non-working residency status for persons who do not need to work. Fee figures, while sourced at the same tier-3 level as the thresholds, are included as evidence_required rather than hard requirements and so do not themselves trigger the draft-sourcing distinction beyond what the thresholds already require.
